record.paper_title: Periods of Integrals on Algebraic Manifolds: Summary of Main Results and Discussion of Open Problems
record.original_question: Which polarized Hodge structures arise from algebraic varieties, including both primitive cohomology of smooth projective algebraic varieties and sub-Hodge structures obtained as images of algebraic correspondences Z on V x V?

evidence.quote: (10.6). PROBLEM***. Which Hodge structures come from algebraic varieties?
we should include all Hodge structures, or equivalently period matrices, which arise from the primitive cohomology
all such Hodge structures should also be considered as coming from algebraic varieties

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A polarized Hodge structure of weight n consists of a finitely generated free abelian group H_Z, a Hodge decomposition H_C = H_Z ⊗ C = ⊕_{p+q=n} H^{p,q} with H^{q,p} = \overline{H^{p,q}}, together with a non-degenerate bilinear form Q on H_Z (symmetric if n is even, skew-symmetric if n is odd) satisfying the Hodge–Riemann bilinear relations: Q(H^{p,q}, H^{p',q'}) = 0 unless (p',q') = (n-p,n-q), and (i)^{p-q} Q(v, \bar v) > 0 for every nonzero v ∈ H^{p,q}.

Say that a polarized Hodge structure (H_Z, H^{p,q}, Q) "comes from algebraic geometry" if it can be obtained in one of the following ways:
(a) as the primitive cohomology PH^n(V, Z) ⊂ H^n(V, Z) of a smooth complex projective algebraic variety V of dimension d, polarized by a hyperplane class L, where PH^n = ker(L^{d-n+1} : H^n(V) → H^{2d-n+2}(V)), with its natural Hodge decomposition and the form Q(α, β) = (-1)^{n(n-1)/2} ∫_V α ∧ β ∧ L^{d-n}; or
(b) as a sub-Hodge structure of such a primitive cohomology cut out as the image of an algebraic correspondence, i.e. the image of the map on cohomology induced by the class of an algebraic cycle Z ⊂ V × V of appropriate codimension.

Problem: Characterize intrinsically (in terms of the linear-algebraic data (H_Z, H^{p,q}, Q) alone) precisely which polarized Hodge structures arise in this way from algebraic varieties.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of characterizing which polarized Hodge structures come from algebraic varieties is a classical open question posed by Griffiths. It remains widely regarded as open; it is closely related to (and in some formulations contains) the Hodge conjecture and questions about motivic realizations. No intrinsic characterization is known, although partial results exist for low weight (e.g., weight 1 corresponds to abelian varieties via the Riemann bilinear relations) and for K3-type surfaces (via the Torelli theorem and surjectivity of the period map).
